title: Eval runner orchestration for profile generation (datasets & prompt registry)
creator: Liam Gallagher
description: Build an extensible eval-runner orchestration layer and dataset/prompt registry integrations to generate reliable performance profiles for model onboarding and version pinning. Current profile generation is brittle: datasets and prompts are referenced ad-hoc within eval scripts, sampling is non-deterministic across runs, and artifact publishing requires manual steps. This ticket will: (1) introduce a lightweight eval orchestrator that runs modular eval runners in parallel with deterministic seeding and stratified sampling; (2) define and implement a canonical prompt-bank schema and dataset manifest (JSONL + metadata) with versioning hooks; (3) add an adapter layer for existing eval runners so they can emit the unified profile output schema; (4) wire automatic publishing to the profile registry (s3://redwood-profiles/) and create a CI job to validate profiles on PRs; and (5) add heuristics for flakiness detection and regression thresholds that feed Console alerts. Focus is on reproducibility, small incremental API changes for runner authors, and minimal runtime overhead for hosted generation jobs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New eval orchestrator (python package) can run 3 existing eval runners in parallel using a canonical runner API and produce a single profile artifact JSONL per model version; 2) Prompt-bank schema implemented with ability to reference templated prompts and canonical slot definitions; 3) Dataset manifest supports stratified sampling, seeding, and per-example metadata (source, dataset_version); 4) CI job validates profile schema + basic quality checks (token latency, top-k correctness) on every PR; 5) Profiles are automatically pushed to s3://redwood-profiles/<model>/<version>/profile.jsonl and a profile registry entry is created; 6) Documentation (Confluence) describing runner contract, schema, and migration steps for runner owners is published; 7) Tests demonstrating deterministic output given fixed seed and manifest; 8) No customer-facing latency regressions introduced by the profile generation pipeline.
comments: 2025-11-04 - Liam Gallagher: Kickoff note. Spent initial day auditing current eval scripts in repo. Found 7 distinct ad-hoc sampling implementations and 4 different prompt encodings. Decided to standardize on JSONL prompt bank and a tiny prompt templating layer (jinja-like).

2025-11-06 - Maya Chen: Prototype of orchestrator landed in feature branch eng/ENG-16789/eval-orch. Orchestrator exposes Runner interface (prepare(), run_batch(), finalize()) and a lightweight registry to discover runner plugins. Initial perf looks good — parallelism with 8 workers reduces wall time by ~3x on local infra.

2025-11-10 - Samuel Ortiz (review): Requested clearer contract for error handling and timeouts. Suggested adding per-run checkpointing so long jobs can resume on infra interruption. Also recommended a canonical metric set to emit (latency_p50,p90,p99; tokens_generated; sample_count; failure_rate).

2025-11-12 - Maya Chen: Implemented deterministic seeding for dataset sampling and added stratified sampler to ensure label balance. Added option to override seed in CI for non-deterministic stress tests.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: we will not adopt a full DVC workflow in this roll-out due to time constraints; instead we version manifests and store canonical dataset snapshots in s3 with checksums. Chose a small runner API to minimize rewrite burden for existing eval owners. Future follow-up: hook registry entries into Console to allow profile browsing and diffing in the UI.
